Job Title:

Medical Coder Professional - Surgical Coder

Job Summary:

Medical Coder-Professional is responsible for reviewing and coding medical records and documentation for healthcare services rendered. This role ensures that all diagnoses, procedures, and services provided are accurately coded using standardized coding systems (ICD-10, CPT, HCPCS). The coder will ensure compliance with insurance requirements, governmental regulations, and industry standards to facilitate correct reimbursement and support the accurate billing process.

Education & Experience

Education and Experience Required:

High school diploma/GED and one (1) year of medical coding experience.


Certifications, Licenses, or Registration Required:


One of the following medical coding certifications from the American Health Information Management Association (AHIMA) or the American Academy of Professional Coders (AAPC):

  • Registered Health Information Management Technician (RHIT)
  • Registered Health Information Administrator (RHIA)
  • Certified Outpatient Coder (COC)
  • Certified Inpatient Coder (CIC)
  • Certified Coding Associate (CCA)
  • Certified Coding Specialist (CCS or CCS-A)
  • Certified Coding Specialist- Physician-Based (CCS-P)
  • Certified Professional Coder (CPC or CPC-A)
  • Any Physician specialty certification from AAPC

Preferred Qualifications:

Prior experience in in trauma, orthopedic, cardiothoracic, wound care, urology, and plastic surgery specialties is preferred.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

Knowledge of electronic coding systems. Proficiency in ICD-10, CPT, and HCPCS coding systems; strong knowledge of outpatient healthcare services and procedures. High level of accuracy and attention to detail in reviewing medical records and assigning correct codes.

Strong verbal and written communication skills to collaborate with healthcare professionals, insurance providers, and internal departments. Proficiency in electronic health record (EHR) systems and coding software.

Responsibilities:

  • Review outpatient medical records to assign appropriate ICD-10, CPT, and HCPCS codes.
  • Ensure coding accuracy and compliance with regulations, payer policies, and guidelines.
  • Work with billing teams to prepare and submit claims, resolving any coding-related denials.
  • Collaborate with healthcare providers to clarify documentation and ensure proper code assignment.
  • Stay current on coding updates and payer requirements.
  • Demonstrative effective communication and response using systems available to both the Hospital Coder and management through telephone and email communication.
  • Demonstrate effective use of required software.
  • The duties listed are general in nature and are examples of the duties and responsibilities performed and are not meant to be construed as exclusive or all-inclusive.

Environmental and Physical Demands:

Requires no exposure to unpleasant or disagreeable physical environment such as high noise level and exposure to heat and cold, no handling or working with potentially dangerous equipment, occasional working hours beyond regularly scheduledhours, occasional travelling to offsite locations, frequent activities subject to significant volume changes of a seasonal/clinical nature, constant work produced is subject to precise measures of quantity and quality, occasional bending, occasional lifting/carrying up to 10 pounds, occasional lifting/carrying up to 25 pounds, no lifting/carrying up to 50 pounds, no lifting/carrying up to 75 pounds, no lifting/carrying up to100 pounds, no lifting/carrying 100 pounds or more, occasional climbing, no crawling, occasional crouching/stooping, occasional driving, no kneeling, occasional pushing/pulling, frequent reaching, frequent sitting, frequent standing, occasional twisting, and frequent walking.(Occasional-up to 20%, frequent-from 21% to 50%, constant-51% or more)

Job Description: Sr. Medical Transcriptionist/ Medical Scribe (Full Time) (Night Shift)

We are currently seeking experienced candidates to join our team as Sr. Medical Transcriptionists/Medical Scribes in a full-time position with night shift hours. This role involves working closely with leading radiologists in the USA, transcribing live and offline dictations across different modalities such as X-ray, CT, Ultrasound, and more. The primary responsibility is to accurately transcribe dictations, prepare reports, and assist radiologists in completing error-free reports.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Transcribe dictations: Listen to radiology dictations and accurately transcribe them into written reports, ensuring precision and clarity in the documentation of medical information.
  • Collaborate with Radiologists: Work alongside radiologists in a live environment, assisting them during procedures and documenting findings in real-time.
  • Offline transcription: Transcribe dictations from audio recordings outside of live settings, taking full responsibility for delivering accurate and timely transcriptions.
  • Prepare reports: Utilize transcribed information to prepare concise and comprehensive reports, maintaining formatting and adhering to specific guidelines.
  • Maintain speed and accuracy: Demonstrate excellent typing skills with a minimum speed of 30 words per minute (WPM) to ensure efficiency in transcribing dictations and report generation.
  • Night shift availability: Exhibit flexibility and willingness to work night shifts in alignment with our operations.
  • Strong communication skills: Possess effective written and spoken communication skills to collaborate with radiologists and other team members, ensuring clear and accurate documentation.
  • Basic computer skills: Utilize computers and relevant software systems efficiently to manage and organize medical records, transcriptions, and reports.
  • Ability to work as a team: Collaborate effectively with the healthcare team, supporting and assisting colleagues to ensure smooth and error-free operations.
  • Continuous learning: Show enthusiasm for learning and adapting to evolving technologies, medical procedures, and guidelines.

Requirements:

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in Medical Transcription.
  • Medical transcription certification or prior experience in the field is highly desirable.
  • Good communication skills, both written and spoken, to effectively interact with radiologists and team members.
  • Strong listening skills to accurately transcribe dictations and capture essential details.
  • Typing speed of over 30 words per minute (WPM).
  • Comfortable working night shifts in alignment with our operational requirements.
  • Basic computer skills, including proficiency in relevant software applications for documentation and record management.
  • Demonstrated ability to work well in a team environment and contribute collaboratively.
  • Immediate availability for joining.
  • Virtual interview process will be conducted.

If you possess a minimum of 2 years of experience in Medical Transcription, have excellent communication and listening skills, and are ready to work night shifts, we encourage you to apply for this challenging and rewarding position. Join our dedicated team and work closely with leading radiologists in the USA, contributing to the accurate and efficient generation of medical reports.

At Verastem Oncology, we address urgent needs of patients living with cancers driven by RAS/MAPK pathway mutations, a key driver of tumor growth and treatment resistance. Position Summary

The Associate Director, Medical Training & Medical Information is a key member of the Medical Affairs organization and serves as the central point of contact for accurate, balanced, and compliant medical information to healthcare practitioners and other external stakeholders, as well as internal stakeholders. This role is has two key areas of responsibility: 1) support the design, delivery, and continuous refinement of scientific, disease state, product, and capabilities training strategies for Medical Affairs, with a particular focus on ensuring Field Medical colleagues have the knowledge, resources, and materials necessary to communicate accurate, balanced, and scientifically rigorous medical information; and 2) manage the day-to-day Medical Information operations, including responses to unsolicited medical information requests, content strategy, vendor oversight, and adverse event and product quality complaint intake and reporting.

The role will partner closely with Medical Affairs, Field Medical, Regulatory, Clinical Development, Safety/Pharmacovigilance, Commercial, Legal, Compliance, and other cross-functional teams to ensure medical information responses, field medical materials, and training content are accurate, compliant, timely, and aligned with approved product information.

Medical Training & Field Medical Enablement

  • Partner with Medical Directors and Field Medical leadership to identify content or training needs based on evolving scientific data, field insights, medical information inquiries, and changes to product information.

About the Role

We are looking for a detail-oriented and knowledgeable Medical Scribe to support healthcare providers with clinical documentation and administrative workflows during patient consultations.

In this role, you will work closely with physicians to document patient encounters in real time, prepare medical charts before appointments, assist with entering orders under physician instruction, and ensure clinical records are accurate, complete, and organized.

The ideal candidate has a strong understanding of medical terminology, excellent typing and listening skills, and experience working with electronic health records (EHRs). You should be comfortable working in a fast-paced clinical environment where accuracy, efficiency, confidentiality, and attention to detail are essential.

Requirements

Key Responsibilities

Real-Time Clinical Documentation

  • Accompany physicians during patient consultations and examinations to document clinical encounters in real time.
  • Record the patient's chief complaint, history of present illness, relevant medical history, physical examination findings, and assessment and treatment plan.
  • Accurately capture clinical information while listening to conversations between healthcare providers and patients.
  • Adapt to different physicians' documentation preferences and workflows.

Pre-Visit Chart Preparation

  • Review patient medical records before consultations.
  • Check medication lists, previous clinical notes, pending laboratory results, and imaging reports.
  • Ensure relevant information is available to the physician before the appointment.
  • Identify missing information or outstanding results that may require follow-up.

Orders & Referral Entry

  • Enter laboratory, diagnostic imaging, and other medical orders under the direct instruction of the physician and in accordance with approved procedures.
  • Assist with entering referrals and prescription information as authorized.
  • Ensure all entries are accurate and flag discrepancies or missing information for the provider's review.

Post-Visit Documentation & Chart Closure

  • Review and organize clinical notes following patient consultations.
  • Assist with visit summaries and supporting documentation.
  • Identify incomplete sections and flag records requiring physician review, correction, or signature.
  • Help ensure patient charts are completed accurately and within the required timeframes.

Coding, Compliance & Confidentiality

  • Ensure documentation captures the clinical details required to support accurate medical coding and billing.
  • Follow applicable patient privacy, confidentiality, and healthcare documentation requirements.
  • Maintain the accuracy and integrity of electronic medical records.
  • Handle sensitive patient information responsibly and in accordance with applicable privacy regulations, including HIPAA where relevant.

Clinical Workflow Support

  • Assist with patient flow by keeping documentation up to date and helping reduce administrative backlogs.
  • Manage multiple documentation tasks and outstanding items efficiently.
  • Communicate with physicians and relevant clinical staff regarding incomplete records or documentation discrepancies.
  • Maintain organized records and follow established clinical workflows.

Minimum Requirements

  • Previous experience as a Medical Scribe or in a closely related clinical documentation role is preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, common diagnoses, and clinical abbreviations.
  • Experience using electronic health record (EHR) systems such as Epic, Cerner, Allscripts, or similar platforms.
  • Excellent typing speed and accuracy; a typing speed of 60–80 words per minute is preferred.
  • Strong written English skills and the ability to produce clear, accurate clinical documentation.
  • Excellent listening skills and the ability to capture relevant clinical details during live consultations.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to identify missing or inconsistent information.
  • Understanding of patient confidentiality and healthcare privacy requirements.
  • Ability to work efficiently in a fast-paced healthcare environment.

Essential Skills & Competencies

  • Clinical documentation: Ability to accurately capture patient information and physician instructions.
  • Medical terminology: Familiarity with common clinical terms, diagnoses, medications, and procedures.
  • Attention to detail: Ensures accurate documentation of medication dosages, clinical findings, and patient history.
  • Active listening: Distinguishes important clinical information from general conversation.
  • Time management: Completes documentation promptly while managing multiple tasks.
  • Adaptability: Adjusts to different physician preferences, specialties, and documentation workflows.
  • Confidentiality: Handles sensitive medical information professionally and securely.
  • Communication: Works effectively with physicians and clinical teams to resolve documentation gaps.

What Success Looks Like

  • Patient encounters are documented accurately and in real time.
  • Clinical notes are complete, clear, and organized.
  • Medical orders and referrals are entered correctly under physician instruction.
  • Incomplete records are flagged promptly for provider review.
  • Patient information remains confidential and is handled in accordance with applicable regulations.
  • Documentation is completed efficiently, supporting smooth clinical operations and reducing administrative backlogs.

Important Note

The Medical Scribe supports the physician by documenting clinical information and carrying out authorized administrative tasks. Clinical decisions, diagnosis, treatment recommendations, and final approval or signature of clinical records remain the responsibility of the appropriately licensed healthcare provider.

If you have strong medical terminology knowledge, excellent attention to detail, and experience supporting clinical documentation, we encourage you to apply.
